column1: # Curated help for the keys worth explaining. Hand-written, and deliberately NOT
# produced by gen-schema.py: that file is regenerated from a device and would
# overwrite anything written here. Merged with it by name, in the browser.
# The rows for keys in settings.tsv describe what the odi-oss image does with
# them. The rest describe the stock firmware -- /etc/runomci.sh for how a key
# reaches omci_app, and measurement for the rest -- and are shown only in the
# read-only stock-keys view. Where a claim is not grounded it says so rather
# depends  KEY=VALUE, joined by &. When unmet the UI says the key is ignored,
#          because that is what the firmware does with it.

column3: help

Becomes `omci_app -t`. Anything outside the listed values falls back to bridge. Switching between HGU and SFU also needs a CS factory reset — this key alone leaves a stale WAN entry behind and the ONU keeps running as a router.

Bitmask, DECIMAL -- `flash set` accepts nothing else. Passed as `omci_app -cr`. Each bit loads one plugin from lib/features; the field below decodes it. Bit 0x4 is `ignore_conn_uniNode_check`, which suppresses the ME 171 uniNode association check; the stock firmware ships with 4. On the 2024 firmware that same bit also skips populating the resolved association, which stops the ONU forwarding at all.
Bitmask, DECIMAL. Passed as `omci_app -cb`. Each bit loads one plugin from lib/features; the field below decodes it against this image.

Bitmask, DECIMAL. Passed as `omci_app -cme`. Bit 0x100 is `cf_apply_customized_veip_slot_id`, which is what makes OMCI_VEIP_SLOT_ID take effect at all -- set the slot id without this bit and nothing happens.
Bitmask, DECIMAL. Passed as `omci_app -cmc`. Each bit loads one plugin from lib/features; the field below decodes it.
1 starts omci_app with `-m enable_wq`.
Answers OK to OMCI operations the stack cannot actually satisfy. Some OLTs refuse to finish provisioning without it.
Read by boa, configd, led, mib and xmlconfig — and NOT by omci_app or checkomci. It does not affect provisioning, which was confirmed from the binaries rather than assumed.

Passed to omci_app, and read as a single byte -- so the MSB of the entity id you want, 14 for 0x0e01, not the whole id. It does nothing on its own: bit 0x100 of OMCI_CUSTOM_ME loads `cf_apply_customized_veip_slot_id`, and without that bit the value is ignored. 255 is the default here; whether the OLT ends up bridged to the VEIP or the physical UNI is what it provisioned on ME 47, not this key alone, unless OMCI_CUSTOM_ME bit 0x100 is set.

Handed to the europa driver at boot by insert_europa.sh, and read by runsdk.sh to choose which stack starts. This key is not only yours: with PON detection on, pondetect rewrites it and reboots after about 24 seconds of light without PON sync, so a value that changed on its own came from there.
The first four characters of the serial number, and must match it.
32 hex characters.
1 is the shipped value.
The device login for SSH and telnet. Not this UI's password, which lives in /etc/config/confd.auth.
The device login for SSH and telnet.

The VLAN untagged frames are placed in on the host-side switch port. Upstream issue #475 reports setting this to 0 as the fix for an ONU that registers but forwards nothing; the shipped values are confirmed to forward correctly on their own, so this is recorded as untried rather than recommended.
As above, for the second switch port.
Whether the resolver addresses below are used or taken from the upstream connection.
column4: 0=0 — from upstream|1=1 — use the addresses below

column3: Writes the decoded OMCI conversation with the OLT. 2 is the parsed form, landing in /tmp/omcilog.par — about 95 KB for a full registration. Reading that exchange is the only way to see what the OLT is actually asking for.
Which message types to log. 4294967295 logs everything.
Leave at 0. /tmp is an unbounded RAM disk on a device with about 1.5 MB free, so the debug level can exhaust memory; parsed message logging is bounded and is what you actually want.
column4: 0=0 — errors only|1=1 — errors|2=2 — warnings|3=3 — info|4=4 — debug (can exhaust memory)

column3: What `pondetect` does with the PON MAC, every two seconds. On: if the SerDes sees light but never achieves sync for about 24 seconds, it concludes the PON type is wrong, rewrites PON_MODE to the other one and hard-reboots -- so a stick that comes back as EPON after a fibre fault did that to itself. Off does not stop pondetect: it still resets the SerDes CDR on every unsynced sample, it just never touches the flash. Detection is skipped entirely while GPON_SN is the factory default RTKG11111111. Read at boot by runsdk.sh, so a change needs a reboot.
column4: 0=0 — off (CDR reset only, never rewrites PON_MODE)|1=1 — on (may rewrite PON_MODE and reboot)

column3: Never writable here. Like the SerDes mode, getting it wrong can take the link down and with it every way into the device.
The address SSH, this UI and the exporter answer on. Saving moves it at once, and this page with it: note the new address first, or turn on the second address below as a way back.
Netmask for the management address, applied with it.

A second, fixed address beside the first (br0:2), for reaching the stick when the first is changed to something you cannot route to; turning it off removes it at once, and a page opened on it stops answering.
Only used when the second address is on; a change moves it at once, and a page opened on the old one stops answering. 192.168.100.1 is the common choice.

1 lets the manual VLAN below tag the services; any other value means the stick adds no tag at all, whatever the VLAN ID says, and on a line whose OLT accepts only tagged frames the service then stops unless the router tags the service VLAN itself. Applied at once, without re-ranging the ONU.
column4: 0=0 — transparent: no tag, service stops unless the router tags|1=1 — manual: the stick tags (below)

column3: Who tags the service VLAN; with router tags the stick adds no tag, and on a line whose OLT accepts only tagged frames the service stops unless the router tags the VLAN itself. Stick tags: the ONU adds the VLAN ID and priority below to untagged frames upstream and removes the tag downstream. Router tags (transparent): the ONU adds and removes no tag, every VLAN the OLT carries passes to the router, which tags. Only read when VLAN config mode is 1; any other value is router tags. Applied at once, without dropping the fibre link: the ONU stays in O5 either way.
column4: 1=1 — Stick tags|0=0 — Router tags (transparent): service stops unless the router tags

column3: The C-VLAN omcid adds upstream and removes downstream on the services the OLT provisions, your ISP service VLAN; a VLAN the OLT does not carry stops the service at once, while the ONU stays in O5 and looks healthy. Used only when VLAN config mode is 1 AND manual VLAN mode is 1, and only with a priority set too.

802.1p priority bits carried in the tag; keep the value the ISP uses, since an OLT that maps or filters by priority can drop frames with another one. Same gating as the VLAN ID; an empty priority means no manual tag, as on the stock firmware.
What the OLT authenticates; a serial number the OLT does not know keeps the ONU off the line, with no service, until it is set back. Four-character vendor prefix followed by eight hex digits.

An OLT that checks the PLOAM password refuses the ONU with a wrong one, and the service stays down until it is set back. Stored as the hex of an ASCII string, shown decoded under the field. Many OLTs authenticate on the serial number alone and leave this empty; others require it.
The MAC of eth0, its host port and br0.

The logical ONU id a CTC-profile OLT asks for; such an OLT refuses the ONU with a wrong one, and the service stays down until it is set back. Left unset when the OLT does not require one. Cannot be cleared from here: the store refuses an empty value.
The password that goes with the LOID; a wrong one keeps the ONU off a CTC-profile OLT that checks it.
The value omcid actually answers when it differs from LOID. Saving LOID writes this too.
As above, for the password.

What the OLT is told image 0 runs (software image entity, 14 characters at most). An OLT that provisions only the identity it expects can leave the ONU in O5 with management and no service when it reads another value.
What the OLT is told image 1 runs. An OLT that provisions only the identity it expects can leave the ONU in O5 with management and no service when it reads another value.

The equipment id the OLT reads in ONU2-G (20 characters at most). The stock firmware reports IGD. An OLT that provisions only the identity it expects can leave the ONU in O5 with management and no service when it reads another value.

ONU2-G OMCC version, decimal. 128 (0x80) is what this image and the stock firmware report. An OLT that provisions only the identity it expects can leave the ONU in O5 with management and no service when it reads another value.

ONU2-G vendor product code, decimal. 15 is what this image and the stock firmware report. An OLT that provisions only the identity it expects can leave the ONU in O5 with management and no service when it reads another value.

The hardware version the OLT reads in ONU-G (14 printable ASCII characters at most), which some OLTs whitelist. Reported only while the ONU identity switch is on; otherwise the device id. Leave it empty to report the device id: an empty value removes the key. A longer value, or one with a character outside printable ASCII, is ignored whole rather than cut, since a truncated version is a different version. Read by this image, not the stock firmware. An OLT that provisions only the identity it expects can leave the ONU in O5 with management and no service when it reads another value.

What omcid does when the OLT starts a software download to this ONU. Accept answers the download and discards the image; reject refuses it. Either way nothing is installed, flashed or rebooted, and the software image entity only reports the image as activated and committed so the OLT is satisfied. Unset is accept. Read at every download step, so a change is in effect at once. Read by this image, not the stock firmware.
column4: accept=accept — answered, then discarded (the service is not touched)|reject=reject — refused (the service is not touched)

column3: 1 answers a Create, Set or Get of a managed entity class omcid has no model for with success, instead of the standard unknown-entity error; off (0 or unset) keeps the error. Turn it on only for an OLT that stalls its provisioning at such an answer, after logread shows event=unknown_me for the class it stops at. The risk: if that entity carried part of a service (a VLAN rule, a queue, a vendor extension), the part is silently missing while the OLT believes it is in place, so the ONU reaches O5 and looks provisioned while the service may not work, and an OLT that audits the MIB against what it wrote can resynchronise over and over. Check the service afterwards. Read by this image, not the stock firmware.
column4: 0=0 — off (unknown entity, the standard answer)|1=1 — on (answer success; a part of a service may be silently missing)

column3: Lets the OLT reboot the stick over OMCI. Off by default. On, a Reboot of the ONU-G is answered with success and the stick restarts a second later (the fibre is down for the boot); off, it is refused with command not supported. Read each time the OLT sends a Reboot, so a change is in effect at once. Read by this image, not the stock firmware.
column4: 0=0 — off (refuse the OLT reboot)|1=1 — on (the OLT can reboot the stick)

column3: Up to 8 entries, separated by spaces or commas, each CLASS:HEX: the class in decimal (1 to 65535) and the attribute bytes in hex (optional 0x, 1 to 25 bytes), e.g. 200:0x0011aa,201:01020304. omcid answers a Get or Get current data of each class with its bytes, under the attribute mask the OLT asked for. Only a class omcid has no model of its own for is answered: an implemented class is never overridden. A class cannot be listed twice. Empty removes the key. Anything malformed turns the whole key off in omcid, so it is refused here before it is written. Applying re-registers the ONU, so the OLT provisions it again and the fibre service drops meanwhile. The bytes stay on this stick, in odi.conf, are not logged and are redacted from the diagnostics bundle. Read by omcid at start and on SIGHUP, by this image, not the stock firmware.

Whether the host port (the SFP edge, toward the router) runs auto-negotiation. On, the default and what the stock firmware does, negotiates 1000BASE-X with the router; off forces 1000BASE-X full duplex, for a router port with auto-negotiation off. Changed only from Config, Network, Host port, as a trial that reverts by itself after two minutes unless kept; never by Save. A boot whose forced link does not come up runs auto-negotiation and says so; three short power cycles in a row clear it. Read by this image, not the stock firmware.
column4: on=on — negotiate (the default)|off=off — forced 1000BASE-X full duplex

column3: The remote syslog collector, as `host` or `host:port`; empty (the shipped default) leaves remote logging off. Read by this image, not the stock firmware. Letters, digits, dots and hyphens only, optional port 1-65535.

The NTP server, as `host` or `host:port`; empty (the shipped default) leaves the NTP client off. Read by this image, not the stock firmware. Passed to busybox `ntpd -p`, which resolves the string with the shared host2sockaddr/str2sockaddr helper -- a bare host defaults to port 123, and a trailing `:port` overrides it. Letters, digits, dots and hyphens only, optional port 1-65535.
